D001-D008_h001.question:
For the last year or so, my wife keeps saying I’m “always on.” I feel like I’m constantly in motion, even when I’m just in my classroom—pacing, fiddling with markers, getting up and down during prep. I struggle to just sit and grade; I’ll start on one stack of papers, then remember an email, then suddenly I’m rearranging my desk instead. By the end of the day, I’ve half-finished ten different things.

In meetings, I catch myself talking way more than everyone else, jumping in before people finish, going off on tangents. Sometimes my students joke that I “never shut up,” and they’re not entirely wrong. My mind races ahead, and I feel like I have to get it all out before I lose the thought.

I’m also really easily thrown off. A noise in the hallway, a kid tapping a pen, or even my own random thoughts can pull me away from what I’m doing. Some weeks I feel more amped up than usual—like I’ve got extra energy and less need for sleep—other times I’m just tired but still restless and scattered. It’s getting harder to manage my workload and keep things straight.
D001-D008_h001.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D001-D008_h001.answer: D & C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Bipolar I Disorder

D001-D008_h002.question:
I’d say this has been going on noticeably for maybe the last year or so, though I’ve always been a bit like this. Lately at work, I really struggle to keep track of my cases and paperwork. I start one assessment, then see an email come in, then remember a phone call I need to make, and suddenly I have three things half-finished and nothing actually done. My desk and schedule feel like chaos, even when I try color-coding and lists.

I get pulled off track so easily—someone walking past my office, a notification, or even just my own thoughts spinning off in another direction. Sometimes I’m thinking about five different clients at once, and I lose the thread of what I was doing.

People tell me I’m “always on,” like I can’t sit still. I’m pacing around the office, tapping my foot in meetings, jumping up to “just check one more thing.” When I’m in that mode, I talk a lot—fast, jumping from topic to topic. Coworkers have gently told me I can dominate conversations, and sometimes I don’t realize how much I’ve been talking until I see their faces.
D001-D008_h002.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D001-D008_h002.answer: D & C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Bipolar I Disorder

D001-D008_h003.question:
I’ve been having a hard time keeping myself together on the road, especially these last few months. My route sheets and delivery times get all jumbled in my head. I’ll start planning the order of stops, then something catches my eye or I start thinking about something else, and suddenly I’ve missed an exit or I’m late because I had to double back. Even simple stuff, like keeping my cab organized, just falls apart—I put things down and then can’t remember where, or I start one task and jump to another without finishing.

Lately I feel like I’m running on high gear most of the time. Even after long shifts, I’m pacing around truck stops instead of resting, like I can’t shut my body off. I talk a lot more than I used to—other drivers, clerks, anyone nearby—I’ll just keep going, hopping from one topic to another before they can really answer.

There are stretches where this “amped up” feeling gets stronger for days at a time, then it eases back a bit, but the trouble focusing and staying organized seems to hang around either way.

A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D001-D008_h003.answer: D & C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Bipolar I Disorder

D001-D008_h004.question:
I don’t really know where to start. Since my wife died a few years back, I’ve thrown myself into work, but lately—maybe the last couple of years, worse in the past several months—I just can’t seem to keep things straight.

I maintain old COBOL systems, so everything has to be precise, but I’ll open a ticket, start tracing through the code, and then some random thought pops into my head—like an idea for automating a report or whether I paid the gas bill—and suddenly I’ve got three screens open and I can’t remember what I was originally doing. My desk and inbox are a mess of half-finished change requests, sticky notes, and printouts. I keep telling myself I’ll set up a proper system, but I never follow through.

People at work say I pace the hallway a lot. I feel like I can’t sit still in long meetings; I’m up refilling coffee, checking something on another terminal, just…moving. When I do talk, I catch myself going on and on, jumping between topics, explaining every detail of a bug when nobody asked. Some weeks I feel especially keyed up—like I have to be doing something all the time—and that’s when all this gets even more noticeable.

    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D001-D008_h005.question:

D001-D008_h006.question:
I’d say this really started bothering me around six months ago, though looking back I’ve always been a bit scattered. Lately at work I’ll be halfway through writing a case note and realize I’ve left whole sections blank or mixed up client names. I’ll miss obvious things in forms, like ticking the wrong box, and my supervisor has had to send paperwork back because of “careless” mistakes.  

Even when I’m in a home visit, my mind drifts. I’ll catch myself thinking about three different things while the client is talking, and then I have to scramble to refocus and ask them to repeat themselves. Reading reports is hard—I’ll get through a page and realize I didn’t actually absorb any of it.  

Outside of work, I feel oddly revved up at times. Watching TV with my daughter or trying to read, I’m fidgeting, getting up, starting little projects, talking over her without meaning to. In meetings I sometimes cut people off or answer before they’ve finished their question, and then feel embarrassed.  

Some days I do feel unusually energetic and talkative, sleeping less than usual, but I can’t tell if that’s just stress and coffee or something else.

A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D001-D008_h006.answer: C & B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Bipolar I Disorder

D001-D008_h007.question:

When people ask me questions—at meetings, or even just chatting—I catch myself cutting them off, answering before they’ve finished. Sometimes I’m speaking really fast and jumping from one idea to another, and then a few days later I’ll feel more flat and low-energy, but I’m not sure if that’s just from being tired or stressed.

    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D001-D008_h007.answer: C & B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Bipolar I Disorder

D001-D008_h008.question:
